questions.prompt: Why is placeholder text inside a form field considered harmful to usability?

options.text: It makes the form field look too cluttered.
It takes up too much database storage.
It disappears on typing, which strains short-term memory and stops error checking.
It triggers false warnings in screen reading software.

questions.explanation: Because it vanishes, users cannot look back to verify what information they were supposed to enter.
questions.hint: Think about what happens the moment typing into a placeholder begins.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Identify why placeholders in forms harm usability.

questions.prompt: When is text exempt from minimum contrast rules?

options.text: When it is located in the main body paragraph.
When it is part of a disabled, inactive control.
When a brand color is prioritized above legibility.
When the text is formatted as a primary button.

questions.explanation: Inactive elements are exempt because faded contrast communicates that the element cannot be used.
questions.hint: Consider elements that are not currently allowed to be clicked.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Understand the contrast exemptions for disabled controls.

questions.prompt: How should a designer treat purely decorative text?

options.text: It must always meet the strict 4.5 ratio.
It should be accompanied by an audio description.
It has no contrast requirement if it is not needed to understand the page.
It must be hidden completely on mobile devices.

questions.explanation: Text used entirely as a visual texture and carrying no meaning is exempt from contrast rules.
questions.hint: Ask whether the text matters for comprehension.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Differentiate between essential text and pure decoration.
